title: Pivoting and Tunneling: move through the internal network
description: SSH local/forward/remote port forwarding, SOCKS with proxychains and chisel tunnels: from one shell to the whole internal network.

pivoting-y-tunneling-t01-q01.prompt: Which SSH flag creates a LOCAL tunnel: a port on YOUR machine listening and forwarding to a destination only visible from the SSH server?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t01-q02.prompt: You have SSH credentials on 10.10.10.5 (DMZ) and from there an internal web service runs on 192.168.1.20:8080 you cannot see from outside. Write the full command to open it on your localhost:8080.

pivoting-y-tunneling-t01-q03.prompt: Which SSH flag does the INVERSE: exposes a service on YOUR machine to the SSH server's network?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t01-q04.prompt: Which SSH flag raises a dynamic SOCKS4/5 proxy (one port routing to ANY destination reachable by the server)?

2.title: proxychains: any tool through the tunnel

pivoting-y-tunneling-t02-q01.prompt: In which file does proxychains configure its default SOCKS proxy (full Linux path)?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t02-q02.prompt: Write the line you would add to the ProxyList to use the SOCKS5 from the previous task's SSH.

pivoting-y-tunneling-t02-q03.prompt: Why does proxychains NEVER route ICMP (ping), and which nmap option replaces ping for host discovery through the SOCKS?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t02-q04.prompt: Which proxychains mode switches to the next proxy in the list when one fails (ideal when chaining several pivots)?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t03-q01.prompt: What language is chisel written in (giving it the single multi-platform binary you upload to the pivot)?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t03-q02.prompt: Write the chisel CLIENT command on pivot 10.10.10.5 to open a SOCKS5 on your Kali (the pivot connects out to your 443).

pivoting-y-tunneling-t03-q03.prompt: With socat: which option on the pivot forwards a local port to another host (a minimal 'port forward' relay)?

pivoting-y-tunneling-t03-q04.prompt: What KEY advantage does chisel's reverse mode (--reverse) have in networks with strict egress firewalls?
